messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PD Alert fired: PD#PD-9821 - gpu_mem_spill_rate > 0.8 on pool infer-prod-eu-4. Metric details attached.
IncidentBot: sample log -> 
```
2026-06-12T14:00:03Z WARN kernel: cuda: memory accounting: vmem_spill 82% (burst)
model-infer-07: CUDA error: allocation failed (size=1.2G) 
```
Alex (oncall): ack'd. I'm on it, will assess blast radius.
Maria: seeing elevated 503s from our dedicated tenant "KestrelPay" on eu region dashboards. They hit ~5% error rate on /v1/generate.
Tim: confirm - autoscaler reported GPU reclaim events and a few container restarts on infer-prod-eu-4.
Ash: @Alex can you divert new traffic from that pool to the cpu-fallback pool or smaller model variants? Might be faster than draining GPUs.
Alex (oncall): routing rule in progress. Running CLI: `redwood route set --pool infer-prod-eu-4 --drain --fallback cpu-fallback-eu`
Alex (oncall): also reducing concurrent batch size for heavy routes: `redwood config apply --route /v1/generate --batch_size 1`
Maria: KestrelPay says they have 2 in-flight requests that timed out. Noticing retry storms from their SDK.
Tim: adding a short circuit to block noisy client retries: `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m string --algo bm --string "retry" -j DROP` (just kidding) -- instead will enable 429-based throttling at edge.
Ash: logs show a repeating host OOM-to-driver-message: `Tensor memory spilled to host (nvml-report) -> vmem spike -> driver fails to free small allocations` — sounds like memory fragmentation + large attention window batches.
Alex (oncall): Escalating to SRE lead if traffic doesn't stabilize in 3m. Maria, please message KestrelPay support with: short note + ETA.
Maria: emailing now: "We're investigating increased errors in EU; routing changes and mitigations in progress. ETA ~10m, will follow up." :email:
PagerDuty: PD-9821 acknowledged by Alex (oncall) at 2026-06-12T14:01:10Z.
Tim: mitigation step 1 complete: pool set to drain, new allocations disabled. Step 2: scaling up small-capacity fallback (2x) for ~3k rps.
Alex (oncall): performing rolling restart on nodes showing fragmentation: `kubectl rollout restart ds/infer-gpu-node -n inference` (doing 2 at a time).
Ash: quick check: are these nodes running older kernel module versions? I see mixed libcuda 525 vs 530 across nodes which can affect reclamation behavior.
Alex (oncall): patching scheduling to avoid older nodes for now. `nodeSelector: gpu.driver=530` applied to new pods.
Tim: observed 503s drop to 0.8% after rerouting. KestrelPay errors decreased to 0.6%.
Maria: KestrelPay sent a follow-up: "Thanks for the quick response, we saw a couple of failed payments but most retried okay." We'll capture customer impact in the postmortem.
Alex (oncall): PD still open. If stable for 15m we'll resolve. Please keep logs and spans for the affected timeframe (14:00:00 - 14:10:00Z).
Ash: note for post-incident: add an eval prompt set to detect memory-spill patterns (long contexts + large batch) and recommend quantization or auto-fallback earlier.
Tim: creating a short runbook task: reduce batch_size on high-context routes automatically when vmem_spill_rate > 0.5.
IncidentBot: PD-9821 status: acknowledged -> in_progress.
Alex (oncall): Marking customer impact: partial (KestrelPay ~5% of requests briefly), no data loss, no SLO breach yet but near threshold.
Maria: copying support ticket #SUP-4472 into incident notes.
PagerDuty: PD-9821 resolved by Alex (oncall) at 2026-06-12T14:12:20Z (reason: pool drained + traffic reroute + restarts).
Alex (oncall): Closing thread. Follow-ups: 1) inventory GPU driver versions and coordinate a rolling upgrade to unified 530. 2) implement auto-batch-down on vmem_spill. 3) add alert suppression for transient spill bursts to avoid noisy PDing.
Tim: will file infra tickets and a short postmortem doc.
Maria: will do customer follow-up and capture exact error counts for SLA reporting.
Ash: jotting a note: possible kernel memory fragmentation bug -> add to research backlog.
Alex (oncall): thanks team :thumbsup: We'll reconvene for the postmortem tomorrow.
